title: Sum of Two Integers
pattern: Add with XOR, carry with AND
statement: Return the sum of two integers `a` and `b` **without using `+` or `−`**.

example.why: 5 + 3 = 8, obtained with XOR, AND and shifts only.

idea: Look at one binary column: `0 + 0 = 0`, `0 + 1 = 1`, `1 + 1 = 0 carry 1`. Ignoring the carry, that is exactly **XOR**. So `a ^ b` adds every column without carries.
A carry arises precisely where **both** bits are 1 — that is `a & b`. A carry belongs one column to the left, so shift it: `(a & b) << 1`.

The true sum is *(sum without carries) + (carries)* — another addition. Repeat with those two numbers until there are no carries left. (The mask keeps the numbers within 32 bits, because Python integers never overflow.)

complexity.timeWhy: At most 32 rounds, because every round moves the carries one bit to the left.
complexity.spaceWhy: Only the two numbers a and b are stored.

steps.text: Our example: **`a = 5, b = 3`**. Each step runs one highlighted line of the code.

steps.text: `a ^ b` adds each column while ignoring carries; `(a & b) << 1` collects the carries, moved one column left. The two masks only serve to imitate 32-bit integers.

views.title: a ^ b = sum without carries      (a & b) << 1 = the carries

steps.text: Sum without carries: 5 ^ 3 = **6**. Carries: (5 & 3) << 1 = **2**. The true total is 6 + 2, which is again an addition — so repeat with these two numbers.

views.title: a ^ b = sum without carries      (a & b) << 1 = the carries

steps.text: Sum without carries: 6 ^ 2 = **4**. Carries: (6 & 2) << 1 = **4**. The true total is 4 + 4, which is again an addition — so repeat with these two numbers.

views.title: a ^ b = sum without carries      (a & b) << 1 = the carries

steps.text: Sum without carries: 4 ^ 4 = **0**. Carries: (4 & 4) << 1 = **8**. The true total is 0 + 8, which is again an addition — so repeat with these two numbers.

views.title: a ^ b = sum without carries      (a & b) << 1 = the carries

steps.text: Sum without carries: 0 ^ 8 = **8**. Carries: (0 & 8) << 1 = **0** — no column produced a carry this time.

views.title: a ^ b = sum without carries      (a & b) << 1 = the carries

steps.text: There are **no carries left** (b = 0), so `a` now holds the complete sum.

steps.text: `a` = 8 fits into a signed 32-bit integer as it is → **8**.
